Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Putting a short operational proposal below to make the steps concrete.

Summary proposal (short):
1) Ownership proof: prefer a TXT-based proof for split-horizon private domains if you can write DNS records in the authoritative zone. If DNS updates are not possible for those private zones, we can do a CSR-exchange + signed ACK via your security mailbox.
2) CSR flow: we provide a CSR template (attached: csr-template.pem.txt). You generate a CSR on your side (key stays with you if you choose customer-managed KMS) and upload the CSR to our secure exchange. We sign and return the certificate bundle.
3) Key custody options:
   - Customer-managed KMS (recommended for higher compliance): you keep the private key in your KMS/HSM. Redwood only receives CSR and returns cert.
   - Redwood-managed escrow: you provide a PKCS#12 export via the secure channel; Redwood stores it encrypted and rotates per SLA.
4) Rotations & automation: we can support ACME for private issuers if you host an internal ACME endpoint. Otherwise, we’ll run a scheduled CSR rotation workflow triggered by the certificate TTL.

Immediate asks from your side to unblock:
- Confirm the list of private FQDNs (ideally in one CSV)
- Tell us whether you can provision TXT records in the authoritative view for those FQDNs
- Policy choice on key custody (KMS vs Redwood escrow)

I’m copying Ben to loop in procurement/timeline. Marissa will outline the technical automation options and failure modes in a follow-up.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical write-up for the options Lauren outlined. Attaching a short Ops doc (dns-verification-instructions.pdf) and a sketch of an ACME-based rotation (acme-lifecycle.md).

Option A — TXT challenge (preferred when authoritative private DNS writable):
- We provide a unique token per FQDN. Your DNS admin creates a _redwood-verification TXT record in the authoritative zone for the private view.
- Once TXT is present, we validate and issue cert. Validation is logged and stored in our audit trail (screenshot/proof stored in the exchange).
- Pros: auditable, no private key exchange. Cons: requires DNS write access to the authoritative private zone (split-horizon ops).

Option B — CSR-exchange (no DNS access):
- You generate CSR using your KMS (command examples in csr-template.pem.txt).
- Upload CSR to our exchange (S3/ signed URL). We validate subjectAltNames against your provided inventory + security contact ACK.
- We return the signed cert bundle. Key never leaves customer KMS if you choose that.
- Pros: works when DNS changes not feasible. Cons: needs additional attestation step.

Edge cases & mitigations:
- Overlapping zones: if two teams claim the same private suffix, we’ll require an ops contact and cross-ownership approval before issuing.
- Split-horizon TTL mismatch: recommend short TTL during rollout to avoid stale records.
- Client trust: we will provide a CA bundle or intermediate that your clients can pin to avoid relying on global trust stores.

Operational cadence proposal:
- S1: Inventory & ownership confirmation (you)
- S2: Verify TXT or upload CSR (you)
- S3: Issue certificate & post back artifacts (us)
- S4: Smoke test in staging (you)
- S5: Cutover & rotate in production (coordinated)

If you prefer ACME, we can run a short connector that hits your ACME server in the private network and performs issuance without any TXT/CSR handoff. That requires a small outbound-only tunnel from a Redwood agent into your VPC (we can sign an NDA and provide a per-connection key).

Thanks — happy to pair on a quick runbook.

— Marissa
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alice — short answers and next steps.

- TXT token format & TTL: token format example in dns-verification-instructions.pdf (we use redwood-<txn-id>=<sha256>). Tokens expire after 72 hours; we will reissue if needed. Recommended TXT TTL: 60s for rollout window, then 300s once stable.

- Attestation for CSR-exchange: an email ACK from the listed security contact is sufficient for initial issuance; for higher assurance we accept a signed PKCS#7 attestation or a signed statement on an internal SSO-backed document (we can accept either). We’ll log the attestation in the audit trail.

Proposed cadence to finalize this:
1) Today: FinMark confirms FQDN CSV (action: Alice)
2) By Nov 5: FinMark indicates custody mode (KMS or escrow) and DNS writable yes/no (action: Alice / ops)
3) Nov 8 call: 30-minute handshake (participants: Lauren, Marissa, Alice, FinMark DNS lead) to validate tokens and walk CSR examples (calendar invite sent)

Thanks — Lauren
